title: RDS: per-request routing service with variant mapping, cache-warm failover, and statistical auto-rollback
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Overview:
Implement a Routing Decision Service (RDS) that makes per-request routing decisions during model deployments and experiments. RDS will evaluate model-variant compatibility, region affinity, capacity tier constraints, and KV-cache locality to select the best target for each request and execute tiered failover when the preferred option is unavailable. The service must support canary rollouts, deterministic A/B bucketing, shadow duplication for validation, and automated rollback triggers based on latency and quality regressions.

Goals:
- Deterministic bucketing for A/B and canary so sticky sessions reuse KV cache and preserve chat context locality.
- A compact compatibility score computed at model onboarding and exposed to RDS for quick routing decisions.
- Tiered failover chain: same-region compatible variant -> same-region lower-tier (quantized) variant -> nearby-region compatible variant with metadata-tagged latency-sla warning -> degraded-response queue/backpressure.
- Transparent shadow traffic path that duplicates traffic to the candidate variant without affecting SLOs and surfaces diffs to the quality dashboard.
- Auto-rollback policy using rolling-window statistical checks (covariate-adjusted p95 latency and prompt-set quality regressions) and circuit-breaker backoffs.

Key Design Points:
- Compatibility scoring: offline process scores model variants on API/IO compatibility (tokenizer, structured output schema, function-calling surface). RDS uses threshold-based gating and an override matrix for admin exceptions.
- Bucketing: 128-bit hash on stable client id or conversation id -> RFC-compliant bucket assignment. Buckets map to cohort assignments for AB tests and persist across sessions for sticky routing.
- Shadowing: configurable sampling rate and header-injection to mark shadowed requests. Observability pipeline tags shadowed responses for differential evaluation without counting towards quota.
- Warm failover: when routing to a different variant that requires KV cache, RDS will perform an async pre-warm probe (cold-key touch) if capacity allows and prioritize requests with low time-to-first-byte impact.
- Rollback triggers: two independent signals (latency SLO breach and quality delta on golden prompt-set). Use Holm-Bonferroni corrected sequential testing over 10-minute windows; immediate circuit open if a single high-severity error class (inference crash, NA output) exceeds threshold.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for bucket determinism and compatibility gating.
- Integration test: simulated canary (1% -> 5% -> 25%) with shadowing enabled and automated rollback under injected degradation.
- End-to-end perf: median added decision latency < 4ms in p50 and p95 < 12ms under normal load.
- Dashboard: new per-cohort rollout page and differential quality summaries (prompt-set pass rate, BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics for structured outputs).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flagged RDS logic in staging with internal policy defaults and shadow-only mode.
2) Closed beta with two customers and internal product teams; monitor cost/latency and rollback signals for 2 weeks.
3) Gradual open rollouts by model owner opt-in, canary percentages ramp as: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Complexity: richer routing improves economics but adds decision latency; we must measure end-to-end impact and provide an opt-out bypass switch for ultra-low-latency routes.
- Data residency: cross-region failover may violate contractual constraints for some customers; RDS needs tenant-level global-routing allowlist.
- Cache warmup cost vs latency savings: pre-warm probes consume GPU cycles; need heuristics to trade probe frequency against expected request savings.

updates: 2026-02-27: Initial spike completed. Proved deterministic bucketing with conversation_id and client_id. Prototype adds 2.8ms median to request path in local env.

2026-03-08: Integration test harness wired to chaos runner; injected 15% latency and observed automatic circuit open behavior. Need to tune sensitivity of statistical tests to avoid false positives during bursty traffic.

Next steps: finish admin override UI, add tenant-level allowlist enforcement, tune rollback thresholds based on closed-beta telemetry, and write migration guide for model owners.
